brief: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows $17 billion in quarterly revenue against $895 billion in compute commitments.
Voters pushed back on data centers in the midterms, and OpenAI responded by pledging to pay full power costs.
AI-driven bug hunting hit core infrastructure: Claude found critical Xen flaws and OpenAI's pipeline produced 948 Linux root exploits.

stories.title: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows $17B quarter and $895B compute bill
stories.snippet: Anthropic's amended S-1 reports about $17 billion in Q3 revenue and a $23.3 billion quarterly net loss. It lists $895.4 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments, $70 billion due within 12 months, ahead of a Nasdaq listing as ANT.
stories.why: The first audited look at a frontier lab's economics shows revenue scaling fast but compute obligations dwarfing it, which sets the bar for every AI IPO after it.

stories.title: Ohio voters pass data-center bans and limits in midterm ballot measures
stories.snippet: Residents of 18 Ohio municipalities voted on 21 data-center measures on November 3, with at least 14 municipalities passing bans or restrictions. A pro-buildout group spent at least $2.54 million on TV ads in the state.
stories.why: Local permission is becoming a hard constraint on AI compute buildout, and siting risk now matters as much as chip supply.

stories.title: OpenAI pledges to pay full power costs at its data centers after vote
stories.snippet: OpenAI published a community compact saying it will cover full electricity and grid infrastructure costs at sites it owns and drop NDAs with public officials. It cites $80 million for Effingham County, Georgia.
stories.why: Labs are now competing on community terms, not just megawatts, to keep data-center projects alive after voter pushback.

stories.title: Xen patches two critical VM-escape flaws credited to Claude
stories.snippet: Xen advisory XSA-523 covers CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704, grant-copy bugs that let a malicious guest read and write other VMs' memory. Every release from 4.6 on is affected; 4.6 to 4.16 get no patch.
stories.why: AI-found bugs in core cloud infrastructure are arriving faster than unsupported versions can be fixed, so patch cadence and upgrade debt now matter more.

stories.title: OpenAI's automated pipeline finds 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits
stories.snippet: OpenAI says its model-driven pipeline scanned about 2.8 million kernel lines, reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and produced 948 working local root exploits, for roughly $1.2 million in API spend.
stories.why: At about $1,300 per bug, offensive-grade vulnerability discovery is cheap enough that defenders should assume attackers can run the same playbook.

stories.title: Anthropic prototypes FlashProve to prove which model produced a reply
stories.snippet: FlashProve uses zkSNARK proofs to show a response came from committed weights without revealing them. On a 400B MoE, one H100 proves about 110 tokens per second, at roughly 70 to 95 times normal GPU cost.
stories.why: Verifiable inference could let API buyers and regulators confirm they got the model they paid for, a missing trust layer for hosted AI.

stories.title: FrontierPhysics: best agent completes 27% of end-to-end physics research tasks
stories.snippet: A new benchmark of 56 tasks built by 42 physicists across nine domains tested 22 models in 26 configurations. No configuration passed more than 46 of 168 rollouts, about 27.4%.
stories.why: Claims of autonomous AI scientists still outrun results; full research loops remain far harder than isolated reasoning questions.

stories.title: Ai2's StateBench shows frontier models lose track of state in long documents
stories.snippet: Ai2's four-level benchmark tests how models follow changing variables across long texts. On the hardest general finite problems, frontier models drop to 13% accuracy or lower.
stories.why: Agents that edit files or manage workflows depend on tracking state over long contexts, and this is a concrete weak spot to test against.

stories.title: Cognition releases SWE-2 Flash, a cheaper and faster coding model
stories.snippet: SWE-2 Flash is a mixture-of-experts model with 276 billion total and 12 billion active parameters, running three times faster at one fifth the price of SWE-2. It scores 20.0 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 27.3.
stories.why: Coding-agent vendors are splitting into fast cheap tiers for routine loops and heavy models for hard tasks, mirroring how teams route work.

stories.title: OpenAI ships ChatGPT Images 2.6 with GIFs and two faster API models
stories.snippet: The update adds animated GIFs in ChatGPT and two API models: GPT-Image-2.6 Flare at about six seconds per image and Sunburst with SVG export. OpenAI says users make over 4 billion images a week.
stories.why: Vector output and faster generation make image models usable inside design and app pipelines, not just chat.

stories.title: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers through App Intents
stories.snippet: A developer preview in the iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 27.3 betas lets any app expose content and actions to Siri AI. App Store submissions open in spring; it is unavailable in the EU for now.
stories.why: Siri becoming an agent that chains actions across apps makes App Intents a key integration surface for iOS developers.

stories.title: Revolut cuts AI coding costs about 90% with self-hosted GLM models
stories.snippet: Revolut made self-hosted GLM models the default coding assistant for about 2,000 engineers, at around a tenth the cost of Claude Code or Codex. It serves GLM on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs.
stories.why: Open-weight models are now good enough for a large enterprise to move default coding traffic off premium APIs, pressuring frontier pricing.

stories.title: Postman Desktop quietly installs plugins into Claude Code and Codex
stories.snippet: A GitHub issue reports that Postman Desktop 12.33.4 adds its own plugins to Codex and Claude Code and writes a hook trust record into global config without asking the user.
stories.why: Third-party apps tampering with coding-agent config is a new supply-chain risk; teams should audit agent hooks and plugin directories.

stories.title: Fal raises $1.3 billion at a $16 billion valuation
stories.snippet: Generative media inference platform Fal closed a $1.3 billion Series F led by Bessemer, doubling its April valuation to $16 billion. The money goes to compute after demand forced it to rate limit customers.
stories.why: Specialized inference clouds are drawing frontier-lab-scale checks, a sign that serving capacity, not models, is the bottleneck for media apps.

stories.title: Anthropic signs first publisher licensing deal, with AP election data
stories.snippet: Anthropic paid the Associated Press for real-time election results that Claude surfaced during the US midterms, its first content deal with a digital publisher. Terms were not disclosed.
stories.why: Anthropic is following OpenAI into paid news licensing, which raises the cost and the quality bar for grounding answers in current events.

stories.title: Chinese tech giants sign a national self-discipline pact for AI agents
stories.snippet: At the Wuzhen World Internet Conference, 20 founding organizations led by state-backed CAICT, including Huawei, Alibaba, Tencent and Xiaomi, released a convention with eight self-regulatory measures for agent development.
stories.why: China is setting agent-specific governance norms through industry pacts, a likely precursor to formal rules builders selling there will face.

coverage: Checked OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta, Microsoft, AWS, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen and Moonshot plus AP, Reuters, Bloomberg, Fortune, Adweek, arXiv and Hugging Face papers; Meta, xAI, Mistral and the Chinese labs were quiet, and openai.com, Reuters, CNBC and Business Insider pages could not be fetched directly.
